title: When the Summit Turns
premise: Oscar Delacroix, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vantors—a family of cheerful, dangerous optimists—runs salvage crews along the monsoon coast, chasing weather systems to stay ahead of the men he owes. When his old rival Maren Kade hires the crew for a run to the Sable Shoals concession, the one job Oscar swore off after the wreck that killed his brother, he takes it because the permits expire in nineteen days and the Vantors' patience expires sooner. The run goes wrong: a leaking boat, a monsoon that won't break, and a stranger named Ilsa Voss who knows too much about the wreck Oscar buried. As the storm traps them and the permits burn down, Oscar must choose between paying his debts with a betrayal or surviving the summit of the season by finally telling the truth about his brother's death. In the end, the boat barely holds, the Vantors are bought off with the concession itself, and Oscar stops running—because staying, for the first time, costs less than leaving.
about_author: Lena Dunmore spent a decade crewing research vessels off the monsoon belt before trading salt water for a writing desk in a harbor town. Her novels blend meteorological obsession with the quiet violence of people who can't afford to stop moving.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days of Good Weather
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He outruns a debt collector through a coastal market while a storm builds offshore, establishing his rule: never stop, never owe twice. The emotional beat is restless denial—he counts days like a man counting exits.

chapters.title: The Vantors Smile
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Dinner with the Vantor family, who discuss his debt with the warmth of relatives and the precision of surgeons. They give him nineteen days. The beat is dread disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: Crew of the Leaky Kestrel
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet his crew: engineer Tomas, navigator Priya, and deckhand Bo, each carrying a reason they can't leave. The Kestrel leaks; so do their loyalties. The beat is found-family friction.

chapters.title: Maren Kade Returns
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Maren, his old rival and the only witness to his brother's wreck, offers a job: the Sable Shoals concession run, the job they swore off. She knows about the Vantors. The beat is old wound reopened.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The crew debates the job; Priya maps the route and quietly decides she needs the money more than the risk. Flashback fragments of the wreck surface. The beat is complicity—everyone knows it's a bad idea.

chapters.title: Signing the Permits
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He signs the concession papers, nineteen days on the clock. Maren watches him flinch at his brother's name on the old documents. The beat is a man signing his own haunting.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Ilsa Voss appears asking passage to Sable Shoals, paying in cash and questions. Bo, the most open-hearted of the crew, vouches for her. The beat is unease wrapped in kindness.

chapters.title: Departure in Gray Light
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. They sail with the monsoon's first edge on the horizon. Oscar and Maren circle each other with a decade of unsaid things. The beat is momentum as anesthesia.

chapters.title: First Squall
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A squall tests the Kestrel and exposes a worse leak than Tomas reported. He hides it, rationing pump time. The beat is the first secret that could sink them all.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Questions
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She probes the crew about a wreck six years old; her knowledge is too precise. She's hunting the truth of what happened to Oscar's brother—and who signed the order that put the old boat out in that storm. The beat is the past closing in.

chapters.title: The Middle of Nowhere Water
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Navigation goes wrong in dead-calm heat; they burn days. Priya realizes someone fed the route a false waypoint. The beat is paranoia—the enemy may be aboard.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession, Part One
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She admits she was on the water the night of the wreck, that the job they're running now is the same concession, same buyer. She stops short of the full truth. The beat is guilt rationed in installments.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Closes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The storm system they've been flanking turns and swallows them. Radio dead, permits ticking. The beat is awe curdling into fear—the weather he loves stops loving him back.

chapters.title: Bailing by Hand
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. The leak wins; the crew bails in shifts through the night. Tomas confesses he hid the damage. Instead of fury, the crew closes ranks. The beat is solidarity forged in bilgewater.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Name
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Revealed: she's the sister of the man who died alongside Oscar's brother, and the concession buyer is the company that falsified the weather report. She came for proof, not passage. The beat is grief with a blade in it.

chapters.title: The Truth About Eli
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, storm-tossed night. He finally admits it: he signed the order that sent the boat out; Maren covered for him for ten years. The beat is the collapse of the story he built his running on.

chapters.title: Summit of the Season
chapters.summary: Full-crew POV rotation in short cuts. The storm's eye passes over them—a false calm at the top of everything—and in that silence they decide: turn back, expose the buyer, or run. The beat is stillness before the choice.

chapters.title: The Back Wall
chapters.summary: Tomas and Priya's POV. They sail through the storm's back wall, Kestrel barely holding, using the monsoon itself to make speed no debt collector could match. The beat is the crew and the sea finally on the same side.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Concession
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At Sable Shoals, they confront the buyer with Ilsa's proof of the falsified report. Maren testifies to what she saw. The beat is truth as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Paying the Vantors
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He trades the concession rights—now valuable as leverage against the exposed company—to settle the Vantor debt. The optimists, delighted by the irony, accept with a smile. The beat is freedom bought by giving up the prize.

chapters.title: What the Storm Left
chapters.summary: Ilsa's and Maren's POV. Names read aloud at the harbor for the dead; Maren and Oscar make no peace, only an honest accounting. The beat is grief that no longer needs to hide.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The Kestrel, patched, stays in harbor. Oscar takes a local job, fixes the leak properly, and lets the crew decide their own courses. Stopping no longer costs more than running. The beat is belonging, finally anchored.
